newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish reserve money up 3.5 bln zloty in Q1 - bank.
newsitem.headline: Polish reserve money up 3.5 bln zloty in Q1 - bank.

text.p: Polish reserve money, the National Bank of Poland's monetary policy operational target, grew 3.52 billion zlotys in the first quarter against a 6.6 billion increase target set for 1997, the NBP said in a report.

The central bank said in its report on monetary policy implementation in the first quarter, that the average reserve money level, used to monitor the system on a short-term basis, increased by 2.075 billion over the period.
"The increase in reserve money in the first quarter of 1997 amounted to 53.3 percent of the assumed growth for the whole year, while the average level amounted to 31.4 percent," the report said.
The bank said an increase in mandatory reserve requirements introduced from the beginning of March accounted for about 1.4 billion zlotys of the increase.

The bank said that after a significant 1.12 billion zloty fall in average reserve money in January resulting from a drop in cash in circulation after a seasonal jump in December, it grew 2.2 billion in February and 3.12 billion in March.

Reserve money, also called high powered money or monetary base, consists of cash in circulation, cash in vaults and obligatory reserves, and has served since January 1996 as the bank's main operational target used to control money supply.
Until the end of last year the bank had been publishing its monthly targets and later report their implementation but since the beginning of 1997 has ceased to do so.
